violated_invariant: Share mint/redeem value must not depend on the pool's instantaneous slot0 price that a caller can move within the same transaction.
notes: Hypervisor.deposit prices shares with TickMath.getSqrtRatioAtTick(currentTick()) and getTotalAmounts(), both read from pool.slot0() with no TWAP or deviation check, and DepositProxy.properDepositRatio compares against the same spot-valued totals, so the gateway adds no protection. Slither only reports unused-return on the slot0 reads (true but not the oracle-trust weakness) and arbitrary-send-erc20 on the V3 callbacks, which are guarded by msg.sender == pool and are not the bug. Hypervisor B (0xc86b...) is a second victim with no prepared candidate.

violated_invariant: Only the SAFE owner (or an address it allowed) can move a SAFE's collateral; a shared library address must never be able to act as owner on behalf of arbitrary callers.
notes: GebProxyActions is a stateless DSProxy action library whose functions carry no authentication because they assume delegatecall; four SAFEs had the library address itself registered as ownsSAFE, so a direct call to quitSystem makes the manager see msg.sender == owner. The code weakness is the absence of a direct-call guard on the library; the registration itself was a user/integration error, so the label is medium-confidence and some reviewers may classify it as misuse rather than a defect. The arbitrary-send-eth findings on freeETH/exitETH describe the same direct-call hazard class but a different function and mechanism, so they are not counted as explaining.

violated_invariant: Free-collateral must correctly reflect a net fCash debt of any magnitude; an unbacked long position must never settle into withdrawable cash.
notes: ERC1155Trade.safeTransferFrom lets any caller mint a payer/receiver fCash pair from an account that holds nothing, and the payer's free-collateral check is the only backstop; ExchangeRate._convertToETH truncates the net balance with an unchecked uint128(balance.abs()) cast, so a ~2^128 debt wraps to a small value and the check passes. The receiver's unbacked claim then settles to cash and is withdrawn from Escrow. All five candidates are proxies whose Sourcify bundle includes the implementation source; the implementation addresses themselves are not candidates and no Slither detector covers unchecked narrowing casts.

violated_invariant: Each share class must be backed by assets accounted to that class only; one raw stETH balance must not back both rsvETH and rsvstETH, and only the owner may register new assets.
notes: The vault prices the rsvETH class off the diamond's raw stETH balance (getRemainingBalance returns balanceOf(vault)), and a permissionless registerErc20(stETH) lets an attacker deposit stETH under a second share class into that same balance, inflating rsvETH redemptions. Only the Diamond forwarding proxy source was recovered; the deposit/register facet is unverified and the InvestmentManagerFacet is not a candidate, so location names follow the PoC and selector matches rather than recovered source. Balancer (0xba12...) in the catalog row is the flash-loan source, not a victim.

violated_invariant: Collateral valuation must not be derived from a price the borrower can set by filling its own orders in the current block.
notes: getMarketUnitPrice returns blockTotalAmount*10000/blockTotalFutureValue for the current block once a small volume gate is met, so a flash-loan-funded cross-account self-trade at par pins the collateral price and lets a cheap lend position be withdrawn against as full collateral. Both candidates are EIP-1967 proxies and only the proxy source was recovered; the TokenVault/LendingMarketController implementations and OrderBookLib are not candidates, so locations come from the PoC's description of verified source rather than this bundle. The incorrect-return/incorrect-modifier findings are the standard transparent-proxy ifAdmin pattern.

violated_invariant: Only the buyer (or an address it authorized) may create an order that moves the buyer's account balance, and the seller written into an order must be validated.
notes: The factory entry (selector 0xbde886fc) checks only getState(buyer)==1, never msg.sender==buyer or a buyer signature, and accepts an attacker-supplied seller; it moves the buyer's whole Account System balance into a new order whose seller-gated abort() then sweeps it. All three contracts are unverified and no candidate has source or Slither output, so function names are the PoC's 4-byte-matched reconstructions and the root cause is inferred from the trace-based PoC only.

violated_invariant: Deposit shares must be minted on a valuation that cannot diverge materially from the market price of the deposited token.
notes: Shares are minted on the oracle-estimated value delta, and the FARM estimator reads a short-window Uniswap V3 TWAP from an imbalanced, thinly traded pool, so FARM bought cheaply on V2 is credited at roughly 9x and the inflated shares are redeemed for the strategy's UNI/AAVE/MKR. Mechanism is recorded as other because the PoC exploits a stale mispricing rather than manipulating the oracle pool itself. The strategy, controller and router proxies have no recovered source and the oracle is not a candidate, so the defect location name is the Enso oracle function the PoC describes, not recovered source.

violated_invariant: AtomicQueue may only pull want tokens from an address that chose to act as solver for this solve.
notes: solve() takes a caller-supplied solver and calls want.safeTransferFrom(solver, users[i], assetsToUser) with no check that solver is msg.sender or consented, so anyone with a standing want-allowance to the queue can be named as solver and drained up to a request the attacker wrote for itself. Slither's arbitrary-send-erc20 finding on that want transfer (index 1) describes exactly this; the offer-side instance (index 0) is the designed, request-gated flow. The catalog's 0x0000...4444 (V4 PoolManager) is only the cash-out venue.

violated_invariant: An ERC-20 transfer(to, amount) issued by a counterparty must move exactly `amount` token units; the same argument must not be reinterpreted as an NFT id that moves a full unit.
notes: O404.transfer treats any valueOrId <= maxTotalSupplyERC721 (50) as an NFT id and moves 1e18 units plus the NFT, so a Uniswap V3 exact-output swap for `id` wei makes the whitelisted pool pay out a full unit for ~2 wei of WETH; the pool is first made owner of low ids by repaying a V3 flash() via the id path. This is inherited ERC-404 design, but pairing it with a whitelisted AMM pool makes it exploitable, hence business_logic. The erc721-interface findings are correct about non-standard signatures but do not describe the dual interpretation.

violated_invariant: Borrow collateral must not be valued at a same-block spot price the borrower just moved, and a same-block guard must bind the actor (contract/position), not tx.origin.
notes: borrow() values deposited SPIRAL with poolManager.getSlot0() spot and lends ETH at LTV_BPS with no TWAP or deviation cap; the only defence, noSameBlockSwap, keys lastSwapBlockOf on tx.origin, so one pump tx followed by six borrows from fresh EOAs through the same attack contract clears the guard each time. Slither failed on the hook candidate (AssertionError, 0 findings), so there is nothing to adjudicate; the Spiral token candidate's findings are all library/informational and unrelated. Deployment block 25949176 is before the fork, so this is pre-patch code.
